title: Endpoint directory response
description: The reply to a trust-gated endpoint-directory query. It lists ONLY endpoints that are simultaneously enabled, actively leased, advertise:true, and admissible for the querying peer. Endpoint identifiers only — no display name, avatar, role, prompt, client kind, payload schema, or permission claim (ADR-0031). Results are advisory and short-lived; a caller may send to an out-of-band EndpointId without querying first.

endpoints.description: At most 32. More than 32 entries, invalid grammar, or duplicates are ProtocolViolation on receipt. A valid but unsorted unique list is sorted locally rather than rejected.

ttl_ms.description: The full wire u32 range is VALID here on purpose. ENDPOINTS.md clamps the effective TTL to min(remote_ttl, local_cache_ttl, 300000) after receipt, and lists only entry count, EndpointId grammar, and duplicates as protocol violations — so an oversized TTL is a tolerated hostile value to be clamped, not a reason to reject the whole response. Asserting the 5-minute ceiling here would turn that into an interoperability failure. Freshness starts at LOCAL RECEIPT, never at generated_at_ms.

generated_at_ms.description: Diagnostic only. Never used for freshness — it is remote-controlled. Bounded by the wire u64 width from `architecture/transport/libp2p/ENDPOINTS.md` so a generated implementation cannot admit an instance that will not encode.
